title: 危化品-乙腈安全使用
hazard_types: 易燃;有毒;刺激性
scenario: 乙腈（HPLC级）的使用
question: 使用乙腈时需要注意哪些安全事项？
answer: 乙腈易燃且有毒，经皮肤吸收、吸入或误食均可中毒（代谢产生氰化物）。操作必须在通风柜内进行，佩戴适当PPE。储存于防火柜，远离氧化剂。废液严禁倒入下水道，须按有机毒性废液分类收集。
steps: 佩戴PPE;确认通风柜正常;在通风柜内取用;用后盖紧瓶盖;存放于防火柜;记录使用量
ppe: 护目镜;丁腈手套（双层）;实验服;必要时佩戴防有机蒸气口罩
forbidden: 禁止在通风柜外操作;禁止靠近火源;禁止与氧化剂混放;禁止倒入下水道
disposal: 含乙腈废液收集于卤代/毒性有机废液桶，按危废处置
first_aid: 皮肤接触：脱去污染衣物，肥皂水清洗;眼睛接触：清水冲洗15分钟并就医;吸入：移至通风处并就医;误食：立即就医，告知乙腈中毒
emergency: 泄漏：消除火源，通风，用惰性材料吸收;火灾：使用干粉、CO₂或抗溶性泡沫
references: 化学品安全数据说明书（SDS）-乙腈; 应急管理部化学品登记中心; https://www.merck.com/products/safety-data-sheets/
source_title: 化学品安全数据说明书（SDS）-乙腈
source_org: 应急管理部化学品登记中心

title: 危化品-甲醛安全使用
hazard_types: 致癌;刺激性;易燃
scenario: 甲醛溶液（福尔马林）的使用
question: 使用甲醛溶液时需要注意哪些安全事项？
answer: 甲醛溶液（福尔马林）具有致癌性（IARC Group 1），对眼睛、皮肤和呼吸道有强烈刺激。操作甲醛必须在通风柜内进行或使用局部排风。佩戴防化手套、护目镜和实验服。孕妇和备孕人员应避免接触。储存于阴凉通风处，与氧化剂和强碱隔离。
steps: 确认通风柜正常;佩戴完整PPE;在通风柜内操作;尽量使用最小量;用后密封并存放于专用柜;记录使用情况
ppe: 护目镜;丁腈手套（甲醛可渗透乳胶）;实验服;必要时佩戴防甲醛口罩或面罩
forbidden: 禁止在通风柜外操作;禁止孕妇/备孕人员接触;禁止与氧化剂混合;禁止敞口存放
disposal: 含甲醛废液按毒性有机废液收集，交有资质单位处置
first_aid: 皮肤接触：大量清水冲洗15分钟;眼睛接触：洗眼器冲洗并立即就医;吸入：转移至通风处并就医
emergency: 泄漏：通风，用惰性吸收材料收集;大量泄漏：撤离并通知专业人员
references: IARC Monographs on Formaldehyde; SDS-甲醛溶液; IARC / 应急管理部化学品登记中心; https://www.merck.com/products/safety-data-sheets/
source_title: IARC Monographs on Formaldehyde; SDS-甲醛溶液
source_org: IARC / 应急管理部化学品登记中心

title: 危化品-二氯甲烷安全使用
hazard_types: 致癌;有毒;挥发性
scenario: 二氯甲烷（DCM）的萃取操作
question: 使用二氯甲烷做萃取时需要注意什么？
answer: 二氯甲烷（DCM）是IARC 2A类可能致癌物，挥发性强，吸入后代谢产生一氧化碳可导致中毒。操作DCM必须在高效通风柜内进行，佩戴丁腈手套（DCM可快速渗透乳胶手套）和护目镜。萃取后废液必须按卤代有机废液分类收集，严禁倒入下水道。
steps: 确认通风柜风速正常;佩戴PPE;在通风柜内进行萃取;废液收集于卤代有机废液桶;用后密封瓶盖;清洁外壁
ppe: 护目镜;丁腈手套（更换频率高，DCM会渗透）;实验服
forbidden: 禁止在通风柜外操作;禁止使用乳胶手套;禁止倒入下水道;禁止敞口存放
disposal: 含DCM废液收集于卤代有机废液桶，按危废处置
first_aid: 吸入：立即转移至通风处并就医（注意一氧化碳中毒可能延迟发作）;皮肤：肥皂水清洗;眼睛：洗眼器冲洗
emergency: 泄漏：通风，用惰性材料吸收;大量泄漏：撤离并报告
references: NIH Working Safely with Dichloromethane; NIH Office of Research Services; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/working-safely-with-dichloromethane.pdf

title: 危化品-乙醚安全使用
hazard_types: 易燃;易爆;麻醉性;过氧化物
scenario: 乙醚的使用与安全
question: 使用乙醚时需要注意哪些安全事项？
answer: 乙醚极易燃（闪点-45°C），蒸气比空气重可沿地面扩散至远处火源引起回燃。长期储存可生成爆炸性过氧化物。操作必须在通风柜内进行，远离所有火源/热源/静电。开瓶前检查生产日期和过氧化物（用淀粉碘化钾试纸测试）。过期或变色乙醚不得使用。
steps: 检查过氧化物;确认通风柜正常且无火源;佩戴PPE;在通风柜内操作;用后充氮气保护并密封;存放于防火柜
ppe: 护目镜;实验服;丁腈手套;防静电鞋
forbidden: 禁止靠近任何火源/热源;禁止用明火加热;禁止敞口存放;禁止使用过期乙醚（可能含过氧化物爆炸物）;禁止蒸馏至干涸
disposal: 含乙醚废液收集于有机废液桶;过期/含过氧化物乙醚应联系专业危废处置
first_aid: 吸入：移至通风处;皮肤接触：肥皂水清洗;眼睛：清水冲洗并就医
emergency: 起火：使用干粉或CO₂灭火器;大量泄漏：消除全部火源，通风，隔离区域
references: 化学品安全数据说明书（SDS）-乙醚; NIH Peroxide Former Guide; 应急管理部化学品登记中心 / NIH; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/managing-peroxide-formers-in-the-lab.pdf
source_title: 化学品安全数据说明书（SDS）-乙醚; NIH Peroxide Former Guide
source_org: 应急管理部化学品登记中心 / NIH

title: 危化品-化学品分类储存原则
hazard_types: 不相容化学品;火灾;爆炸;有毒气体
scenario: 实验室化学品储存管理
question: 实验室化学品应该如何分类储存？
answer: 化学品必须按不相容性分类储存，基本原则：1) 氧化剂与易燃物/还原剂隔离；2) 酸与碱隔离；3) 强酸与氰化物/硫化物隔离（产生有毒气体）；4) 水反应性物质远离水源和潮湿环境；5) 易燃品存放于防火柜；6) 剧毒品双人双锁管理。建议使用化学品储存兼容性矩阵表进行规划。
steps: 整理化学品清单;按危害类别分类（易燃/氧化/腐蚀/有毒/水反应）;查阅不相容性矩阵;分区存放并标注;定期检查容器密封和标签完整性
ppe: 搬运时佩戴护目镜、实验服、手套
forbidden: 禁止氧化剂与易燃物同柜存放;禁止酸与碱同柜存放;禁止化学品存放于地面;禁止食品存放于实验室冰箱
disposal: 过期/废弃化学品按危废分类处置
emergency: 如发生不相容化学品混合：立即停止操作，隔离区域，按应急预案处理
references: NIH Fact Sheet on Compatible Chemical Storage; GB 15603-2022 危险化学品仓库储存通则; NIH / 国家市场监督管理总局; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/fact-sheet-on-compatible-chemical-storage.pdf
source_title: NIH Fact Sheet on Compatible Chemical Storage; GB 15603-2022 危险化学品仓库储存通则
source_org: NIH / 国家市场监督管理总局
tags: 化学品储存;分类;不相容;安全管理

title: 危化品-易燃品防火柜管理
hazard_types: 易燃;火灾
scenario: 易燃化学品防火柜使用
question: 防火安全柜的使用要求有哪些？
answer: 防火柜用于储存易燃液体，柜体应有FM或UL认证。使用要求：1) 柜内总量不超过柜体标称容量；2) 柜门保持关闭；3) 通风口（如有）不得封堵，需连接至排风系统；4) 柜内不得存放氧化剂或不相容化学品；5) 柜体需接地防静电；6) 柜体附近不得堆放杂物。
steps: 确认防火柜完好;化学品分类后入柜;保持柜门关闭;定期检查通风口和接地;每月盘点
ppe: 取用化学品时佩戴护目镜、手套
forbidden: 禁止在防火柜内存放氧化剂;禁止柜门长期敞开;禁止防火柜附近使用明火;禁止超容量存放
emergency: 防火柜周围起火：关闭柜门，撤离并按消防应急预案处理
references: NIH Fact Sheet on Chemical Storage Cabinets; NFPA 30; NIH / NFPA; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/fact-sheet-on-chemical-storage-cabinets.pdf
source_title: NIH Fact Sheet on Chemical Storage Cabinets; NFPA 30
tags: 防火柜;易燃品;储存;消防

title: 危化品-气瓶安全使用通则
hazard_types: 高压气体;窒息;爆炸;低温冻伤
scenario: 实验室气瓶的日常使用
question: 实验室气瓶使用的安全要求有哪些？
answer: 气瓶使用必须遵循以下要求：1) 直立存放并固定在墙上或气瓶架上；2) 瓶帽在不使用时必须盖好；3) 减压阀专瓶专用；4) 可燃气体气瓶需接地；5) 有毒/可燃气体在专用气瓶柜内使用（带排风和报警）；6) 气瓶远离热源（>50°C）和明火；7) 剩余压力不低于0.05MPa。
steps: 检查气瓶标签和检验日期;使用链条/支架固定;安装适配的减压阀;检漏（用检漏液，禁用明火）;缓慢开启阀门;使用后关闭阀门、释放余压
ppe: 搬运时：安全鞋、手套;操作有毒/腐蚀气体时：护目镜、面罩、相应防护手套
forbidden: 禁止倾倒气瓶;禁止使用油脂润滑氧气瓶阀门;禁止将气瓶完全放空;禁止私拉乱接气路;禁止非固定状态使用
disposal: 废弃/过期气瓶交回供应商，禁止自行处理
first_aid: 冻伤（低温气体）：温水复温，就医
emergency: 气体泄漏：关闭阀门（安全前提下），通风，撤离，报告;气瓶倾倒：隔离区域，由专业人员处理
references: GB/T 34525-2017 气瓶搬运、装卸、储存和使用安全规定; 国家市场监督管理总局; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB/T 34525-2017 气瓶搬运、装卸、储存和使用安全规定
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局
tags: 气瓶;高压气体;减压阀;安全操作

title: 危化品-液氮安全使用
hazard_types: 低温冻伤;窒息;压力爆炸
scenario: 液氮的取用与储存
question: 使用液氮时需要注意什么安全事项？
answer: 液氮温度-196°C，可导致严重冻伤。使用要求：1) 佩戴防低温手套和面罩；2) 使用专用液氮容器（杜瓦瓶），不可用普通保温杯替代；3) 在通风良好处操作，防止氮气置换空气导致窒息；4) 液氮容器不可密封（需有泄压口）；5) 避免皮肤和衣物接触液氮。若在密闭空间大量使用液氮，需配备氧浓度报警仪。
steps: 检查容器完好且有泄压口;佩戴防低温手套和面罩;缓慢注入液氮避免飞溅;操作在通风处进行;使用后及时盖好;记录使用量
ppe: 防低温手套;面罩或护目镜;实验服;安全鞋
forbidden: 禁止徒手接触液氮或超低温表面;禁止用密闭容器储存液氮;禁止在小密闭空间大量使用;禁止将液氮倒入水槽
disposal: 剩余液氮在通风处自然蒸发，不得倒入下水道（可能导致管道冻裂）
first_aid: 冻伤：立即将冻伤部位浸入37-40°C温水中缓慢复温，禁止揉搓，就医;窒息：立即移至通风处，必要时给氧
emergency: 大量泄漏：通风，撤离，检查氧浓度;容器破裂：隔离区域
references: NIH Compressed Gas and Cryogen Safety Guidelines; NIH Office of Research Services; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/compressed-gas-and-cryogen-safety-guidelines-document.pdf
source_title: NIH Compressed Gas and Cryogen Safety Guidelines

title: 设备-电泳仪安全使用
hazard_types: 高压触电;化学品暴露
scenario: 凝胶电泳操作
question: 使用电泳仪时需要注意哪些安全事项？
answer: 电泳仪使用高压电源（通常100-300V），存在触电风险。安全要求：1) 使用前检查电泳槽和导线是否完好；2) 确认电泳槽无漏液；3) 先连接导线再接电源，先断电源再拆导线；4) 凝胶中含核酸染料（如EB替代物），操作时佩戴手套，在指定区域进行；5) 跑胶区域明显标示「高压危险」。
steps: 检查设备和导线;配制凝胶（在通风柜/安全区域）;上样;连接导线;盖好安全盖;通电运行;结束后先断电再拆导线;取出凝胶;清洁
ppe: 手套;实验服;护目镜
forbidden: 禁止带电插拔导线;禁止湿手操作;禁止电泳槽漏液时通电;禁止用手直接接触凝胶
disposal: 凝胶按生物危废处理;电泳缓冲液按化学危废处理
first_aid: 触电：先断电，用绝缘物隔离，必要时心肺复苏并就医
emergency: 触电事故：立即断电并报告
references: GB/T 13869-2017 用电安全导则; 国家市场监督管理总局; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局

title: 设备-真空泵安全使用
hazard_types: 机械伤害;化学品吸入;玻璃器皿内爆
scenario: 旋转蒸发/真空抽滤操作
question: 使用真空泵时需要注意哪些安全事项？
answer: 真空泵使用涉及内爆风险和化学品暴露：1) 真空玻璃器皿使用前检查有无裂纹；2) 抽真空时玻璃器皿外部应包裹防护网/胶带防爆；3) 泵出口应连接冷阱或吸收装置（防止挥发性溶剂进入泵体和环境）；4) 使用完毕先释放真空再关闭泵；5) 定期更换泵油。
steps: 检查玻璃器皿有无裂纹;包裹防护网;连接管路;开启冷阱/冷凝器;缓慢开启真空;监控压力;使用后缓慢释放真空;关闭泵
ppe: 护目镜;实验服;手套
forbidden: 禁止使用有裂纹的玻璃器皿抽真空;禁止未包裹防爆网抽真空;禁止直接将有机溶剂蒸气排入泵体;禁止快速释放真空
disposal: 冷阱收集的溶剂按危废处理;废泵油按危废处理
first_aid: 玻璃飞溅伤害：止血、清洁伤口、就医
emergency: 玻璃器皿内爆：立即停止真空，隔离区域，清理碎片
references: 高等学校实验室安全规范（教育部2024）; Prudent Practices in the Laboratory; 教育部 / National Academies Press; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK55873/
source_title: 高等学校实验室安全规范（教育部2024）; Prudent Practices in the Laboratory

title: PPE-手套选择指南
hazard_types: 化学品渗透;过敏;物理损伤
scenario: 实验手套的选择
question: 不同类型的实验手套应该如何选择？
answer: 手套材质选择指南：1) 丁腈手套：通用防化手套，耐多数有机溶剂和酸碱，推荐首选；2) 乳胶手套：舒适性好但不耐多数有机溶剂（易渗透），可能引起过敏；3) 氯丁橡胶手套：耐酸碱和醇类；4) PVA手套：耐强有机溶剂但不耐水；5) 防割手套：处理玻璃碎片或锐器时使用；6) 隔热手套：高温操作时使用。选择时应参考SDS和化学品渗透时间数据。
steps: 查阅SDS确认化学品手套材质要求;选择合适材质和尺寸的手套;检查手套有无破损;戴手套;实验后脱除并洗手
forbidden: 禁止同一双手套在不同实验间混用;禁止手套接触电脑/门把手/电话等公共物品;禁止使用破损手套
disposal: 废弃手套按实验类别（化学/生物）分类处置
first_aid: 手部接触到化学品：脱除手套，立即冲洗
references: NIH Guidance for the Selection of Laboratory Coats; OSHA PPE Standard; NIH / OSHA; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/laboratory-coat-selection-guidance.pdf
source_title: NIH Guidance for the Selection of Laboratory Coats; OSHA PPE Standard

title: PPE-护目镜选择
hazard_types: 飞溅;冲击;紫外辐射;激光
scenario: 眼部防护选择
question: 实验室眼部防护应该如何选择？
answer: 实验室眼部防护分三级：1) 安全眼镜（防冲击）：基础防护，适用于无飞溅风险的常规操作；2) 护目镜（防化型）：用于处理化学品（酸、碱、溶剂），需有侧防护和防雾功能；3) 面罩：高风险的强酸/强碱大量操作、液氮取用等场景。激光操作需佩戴对应波长的激光防护镜。紫外操作需佩戴紫外防护面罩。普通近视眼镜不能替代安全眼镜。
steps: 评估实验的眼部风险;选择对应防护等级的护目镜;检查镜片有无划痕/老化;正确佩戴并确认舒适
forbidden: 禁止用普通近视眼镜替代护目镜;禁止在有飞溅风险时不戴护目镜;禁止使用有划痕影响视野的防护镜
first_aid: 化学品溅入眼睛：立即用洗眼器冲洗15分钟并就医
references: GB 14866-2006 个人用眼护具技术要求; 国家市场监督管理总局; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB 14866-2006 个人用眼护具技术要求
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局

title: PPE-呼吸防护选择
hazard_types: 有毒粉尘;有机蒸气;酸性气体;生物气溶胶
scenario: 呼吸防护的选择与使用
question: 什么情况下需要佩戴呼吸防护设备？如何选择？
answer: 当通风柜/工程控制不足以降低暴露风险至安全水平时，需要呼吸防护。选择原则：1) 防颗粒物口罩（N95/KN95）：防护粉尘、气溶胶；2) 防有机蒸气口罩（含活性炭）：防护有机溶剂蒸气；3) 防酸性气体口罩：防护HCl、HNO₃等酸性气体；4) 全面罩/半面罩+滤毒盒：高浓度或混合危害场景；5) 正压式呼吸器：氧气不足或极高风险环境（需专门培训）。呼吸防护用品须经过适合性测试。
steps: 评估空气中有害物质类型和浓度;选择合适类型和过滤等级;进行佩戴适合性检查;使用后妥善存放和定期更换滤材
forbidden: 禁止在未知污染物或氧含量不足环境中使用过滤式口罩;禁止使用过期或受潮的口罩/滤毒盒;禁止未经培训使用正压式呼吸器
disposal: 废弃口罩/滤毒盒按危废处理
first_aid: 吸入有害物质：移至通风处，必要时就医
references: GB 2890-2022 呼吸防护 自吸过滤式防毒面具; OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard; 国家市场监督管理总局 / OSHA; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB 2890-2022 呼吸防护 自吸过滤式防毒面具; OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局 / OSHA

title: PPE-实验服材质选择
hazard_types: 化学品;火焰;污染
scenario: 选择合适的实验服
question: 棉质实验服和阻燃实验服有什么区别？什么时候需要阻燃实验服？
answer: 棉质实验服适用于大多数常规化学实验，提供基础的化学品飞溅防护。但棉质不阻燃，遇火会燃烧。阻燃实验服（如Nomex材质）适用于：1) 大量使用易燃溶剂（如乙醚、丙酮、正己烷等）的操作；2) 涉及明火或高温的操作；3) 涉及自燃化学品（如叔丁基锂）的操作。选择时还需考虑：阻燃实验服通常比棉质贵但使用寿命更长。
steps: 评估实验中的火灾风险;若大量使用易燃品或涉及明火，选择阻燃实验服;确认实验服合身且能快速脱下;进入实验区前穿好
forbidden: 禁止穿化纤材质的衣物进行易燃品操作（化纤遇火熔化粘在皮肤上加重伤害）
first_aid: 实验服着火：停止倒下滚动，用灭火毯覆盖，或使用安全淋浴
references: NIH Guidance for the Selection of Laboratory Coats; NIH Office of Research Services; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/laboratory-coat-selection-guidance.pdf
source_title: NIH Guidance for the Selection of Laboratory Coats

title: 危废-生物废弃物处置
hazard_types: 生物污染;感染;基因污染
scenario: 生物实验室废弃物处理
question: 生物实验室的废弃物应该如何处置？
answer: 生物废弃物按风险分级处置：1) 一般生物废物（非感染性）：密封包装后按生活垃圾处理；2) 感染性废物（含病原微生物）：必须高压灭菌（121°C, 30min）灭活后方可出实验室；3) 锐器（针头、刀片、破碎玻璃）：放入专用锐器盒，不可混合在普通垃圾中；4) 基因修饰生物废弃物：按生物安全等级规定灭活；5) 动物尸体/组织：专用冷冻暂存，交专业机构无害化处理。
steps: 在产废点分类;感染性废物高温灭菌;锐器入专用锐器盒;动物组织冷冻暂存;填写危废转移联单;交专业机构处置
ppe: 手套;实验服;必要时佩戴口罩和护目镜
forbidden: 禁止感染性废物未经灭活直接出实验室;禁止锐器混入普通垃圾;禁止生物危废与化学危废混合;禁止随意丢弃实验动物尸体
disposal: 按GB 19489和本地危废管理规定处置
first_aid: 锐器刺伤：流水冲洗，消毒，就医评估感染风险
emergency: 感染性废物泄漏：隔离区域，消毒（含氯消毒剂），报告
references: GB 19489-2008 实验室生物安全通用要求; 医疗废物管理条例; 国家市场监督管理总局 / 国务院; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB 19489-2008 实验室生物安全通用要求; 医疗废物管理条例
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局 / 国务院

title: 危废-空化学试剂瓶处置
hazard_types: 化学品残留;环境污染
scenario: 空试剂瓶的处理
question: 用完的化学试剂空瓶可以当普通垃圾扔掉吗？
answer: 不能。化学试剂空瓶内壁仍有化学品残留，必须按以下流程处理：1) 空瓶倒扣沥干（在通风柜内）；2) 瓶内残留量少的三次清洗（清洗液作为废液收集）；3) 去除或涂盖原标签；4) 分类收集（酸瓶、碱瓶、有机溶剂瓶分开）；5) 交由有资质的危废处置单位回收。不得将试剂瓶卖给废品回收站或随意丢弃。
steps: 倒空残留液（通风柜内）;三次清洗（清洗液入废液桶）;去除或涂盖原标签;按类别分装于专用收集袋/箱;贴危废标签;积累一定量后交专业机构
ppe: 护目镜;手套;实验服
forbidden: 禁止作为普通垃圾丢弃;禁止卖给废品回收;禁止残留大量化学品的瓶子不清洗直接封装;禁止不同类别空瓶混合
disposal: 交有资质危废单位回收
references: GB 18597-2001 危险废物贮存污染控制标准; 生态环境部; https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/gtfwyhxpgl/wfhgql/
source_title: GB 18597-2001 危险废物贮存污染控制标准

title: 危废-过期化学品处置
hazard_types: 变质;爆炸;有毒气体;环境污染
scenario: 实验室过期化学品的清理
question: 实验室的过期化学品应该如何处理？
answer: 过期化学品处置是实验室安全高风险环节：1) 定期（每学期至少一次）清理盘点过期/废弃化学品；2) 列表登记品名、数量、危害类别；3) 按不相容性分类打包（氧化剂、易燃品、腐蚀品、剧毒品分开）；4) 由专业人员转运至校内危废暂存库；5) 联系有资质的危废处置单位定期清运。特别注意：过期过氧化物形成剂（乙醚、四氢呋喃等）可能形成爆炸性过氧化物，切勿擅自处理，应联系专业队伍。
steps: 每学期盘点化学品;将过期化学品列入清理清单;按不相容性分类;填写危废转移联单;专业人员打包转运;交有资质单位处置
ppe: 护目镜;实验服;手套;必要时呼吸防护
forbidden: 禁止自行焚烧/掩埋;禁止倒入下水道;禁止未经分类直接打包（不同类混放可能反应起火）;禁止擅自处理过期过氧化物形成化学品
disposal: 交有资质危废处置单位
emergency: 若打包过程中发生反应/冒烟：立即停止，疏散，报告
references: 危险废物污染防治技术政策; NIH Managing Peroxide Formers Guide; 生态环境部 / NIH; https://ors.od.nih.gov/sr/dohs/Documents/managing-peroxide-formers-in-the-lab.pdf
source_title: 危险废物污染防治技术政策; NIH Managing Peroxide Formers Guide
tags: 过期化学品;危废;过氧化物;处置

title: 危废-含重金属废液处置
hazard_types: 重金属;毒性;环境污染
scenario: 含重金属实验废液的处置
question: 含重金属的实验废液应该怎么处理？
answer: 含重金属废液（如含Cr、Hg、Pb、Cd、As、Ni、Cu等）属于危险废物，毒性高，尤其不能进入水体。处置要求：1) 单独分类收集于专用废液桶（不可与有机废液或酸碱废液混合）；2) 废液桶明确标注所含重金属种类和浓度；3) 含六价铬废液需特别注意——六价铬是强致癌物；4) 含汞废液尤其危险（汞蒸气剧毒），密闭存放；5) 满桶后交有重金属危废处置资质的单位处理。
steps: 单独收集含重金属废液;标注金属种类和大致浓度;密闭保存;满桶后联系专业处置;填写危废联单
ppe: 护目镜;手套;实验服;操作汞化合物时在通风柜内进行
forbidden: 禁止含重金属废液与其他废液混合;禁止倒入下水道;禁止用一般化学废液方式处理;禁止敞口存放含汞废液（汞蒸气挥发）
disposal: 交有重金属危废处理资质的专业单位
first_aid: 接触含汞废液：立即冲洗，就医检测血汞水平
emergency: 含汞废液泄漏：隔离区域，用硫粉或专用汞吸收剂处理，通风
references: GB 18597-2001 危险废物贮存污染控制标准; 危险废物污染防治技术政策; 生态环境部; https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/gtfwyhxpgl/wfhgql/
source_title: GB 18597-2001 危险废物贮存污染控制标准; 危险废物污染防治技术政策

title: 应急-灭火器选择与使用
hazard_types: 火灾;爆炸
scenario: 使用灭火器扑救初起火灾
question: 实验室不同类型的火灾应该使用什么灭火器？
answer: 灭火器选择按火灾类别：A类（普通可燃物：木材、纸张）：水型或干粉灭火器；B类（易燃液体：溶剂、油类）：干粉或CO₂灭火器；C类（电气设备）：CO₂或干粉灭火器（先断电）；D类（可燃金属：钠、钾、镁、锂）：专用D类灭火器或干砂（严禁用水！）；K类（烹饪油脂）：湿化学灭火器。实验室最常见的是B类和C类火灾，推荐配备ABC干粉灭火器+CO₂灭火器。使用口诀：提-拔-握-压（提起灭火器、拔保险销、握喷管、压手柄），站在上风方向，对准火焰根部扫射。
steps: 评估火情（仅初起小火可自行灭火）;选择正确灭火器;提灭火器至火源上风方向;拔保险销;握喷管对准火焰根部;压下手柄扫射;确认火已完全熄灭;报告
ppe: 灭火时佩戴防护手套
forbidden: 禁止用水扑灭油类/电气/金属火灾;禁止站在下风方向灭火;禁止使用过期/失压灭火器;禁止灭火后不报告
emergency: 火势无法控制：立即停止灭火，撤离并报警
references: GB 50140-2005 建筑灭火器配置设计规范; NFPA 10; 住建部; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB 50140-2005 建筑灭火器配置设计规范; NFPA 10

title: 应急-触电急救
hazard_types: 触电;电击
scenario: 有人触电时的急救
question: 如果有人触电了，正确的急救步骤是什么？
answer: 触电急救最关键的第一步是确保施救者自身安全。不要直接接触触电者！步骤：1) 立即切断电源（拉闸/拔插头）；2) 若无法断电，用干燥的木棍、塑料棒等绝缘物将触电者与电源分离；3) 检查触电者意识和呼吸；4) 若无呼吸/心跳，立即开始CPR并呼叫120；5) 若触电者清醒，保持平卧保暖并等待急救人员。注意：高压电触电时，即使已断电也保持安全距离（可能有余电），等待专业人员处理。
steps: 确保自身安全;立即断电;用绝缘物分离触电者;检查意识/呼吸;无呼吸心跳则开始CPR;呼叫120;清醒者平卧保暖;陪伴等待急救
ppe: 绝缘手套（如有）
forbidden: 禁止直接接触触电者;禁止用金属/湿物接触;禁止在不确定断电的情况下接近高压触电者
first_aid: CPR直到急救人员到达;烧伤伤口用无菌敷料覆盖
emergency: 立即报告实验室管理人员和安保部门
references: GB/T 13869-2017 用电安全导则; AHA CPR指南; 国家市场监督管理总局; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/
source_title: GB/T 13869-2017 用电安全导则; AHA CPR指南
source_org: 国家市场监督管理总局

title: 应急-化学品中毒急救
hazard_types: 中毒;有毒气体;误食
scenario: 化学品中毒的紧急处理
question: 有人化学品中毒了应该怎么急救？
answer: 化学品中毒分三种途径，急救方式不同：1) 吸入中毒：立即将中毒者移至通风处，保持呼吸道通畅，若呼吸停止开始人工呼吸（注意：氰化物等中毒时不可口对口人工呼吸，使用球囊面罩），尽快就医；2) 皮肤吸收：脱去污染衣物，用大量清水冲洗至少15分钟；3) 误食：不要催吐（腐蚀性物质催吐会造成二次伤害），立即就医并带上化学品容器或SDS。所有中毒急救的第一步是确认施救者自身有防护。
steps: 确保自身有防护（戴手套等）;将中毒者移出污染环境;判断中毒途径;吸入者：通风+观察呼吸;皮肤者：脱衣+大量冲洗;误食者：不要催吐+立即就医;带上化学品SDS或容器就医
ppe: 手套;护目镜;必要时呼吸防护
forbidden: 禁止不做防护直接施救;禁止贸然对腐蚀性物质中毒者催吐;禁止给昏迷者喂水;禁止在不确定化学品的情况下使用「民间偏方」解毒
first_aid: 按SDS急救指引处理;尽快就医
emergency: 拨打120;报告实验室管理人员;保留化学品信息供医生参考
references: 危险化学品安全管理条例; SDS急救指引; 国务院 / 应急管理部; https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1825120.htm
source_title: 危险化学品安全管理条例; SDS急救指引
source_org: 国务院 / 应急管理部

title: 制度-实验室安全标识
hazard_types: 管理缺陷;信息缺失
scenario: 实验室安全标识的识别
question: 实验室常见的安全标识有哪些？分别代表什么意思？
answer: 实验室安全标识按GB 2894分为四类：1) 禁止标识（红色圆形+斜杠）：禁止吸烟、禁止明火、禁止触摸等；2) 警告标识（黄色三角形）：当心触电、当心腐蚀、当心中毒、生物危害、激光辐射等；3) 指令标识（蓝色圆形）：必须戴护目镜、必须戴手套、必须穿实验服等；4) 提示标识（绿色方形）：安全出口、洗眼器、安全淋浴、急救箱、消防器材位置等。每个实验室门口应有安全信息牌，标明本实验室主要危险源、PPE要求和应急联系方式。
steps: 进入实验室前看清楚门口安全信息牌;了解各标识含义;按要求做好防护;牢记安全出口和应急设施位置
forbidden: 禁止擅自撕毁、涂改安全标识;禁止遮挡安全出口指示
references: GB 2894-2008 安全标志及其使用导则; GB 13690-2009 化学品分类和危险性公示通则; 国家市场监督管理总局; https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/

title: 制度-化学品采购与台账管理
hazard_types: 管理缺陷;化学品失控
scenario: 化学品的规范采购和登记
question: 实验室化学品的采购和台账管理有什么要求？
answer: 化学品采购与台账管理要求：1) 采购前评估必要性和替代方案（能用低毒替代高毒吗？）；2) 剧毒品、易制毒化学品、易制爆化学品须经公安部门审批备案方可购买；3) 购买后48小时内录入实验室化学品台账（品名、CAS号、数量、存放位置、采购日期、负责人）；4) 剧毒品实行「五双管理」（双人保管、双人领取、双人使用、双把锁、双本账）；5) 每学期至少盘点一次。

question: Health and Safety Risk for 3D Printers相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: 3D printers pose several health and safety hazards. Main hazards associated with 3D printing are health hazards due to exposure to volatile organic compounds (VOCs), ultrafine particles (UFPs) that fall within the nanoparticle range (smaller than 100 nanometers in size) and exposure to various hazardous chemicals. Exposure can occur during all the stages of printing including pre- printing, printing, post-printing and cleaning/ maintenance. Health and safety hazards depend on the type of 3D printing process and the print material(filament) used. Below are examples of some of the hazards: • Exposure to VOCs and UFPs including particles in nanomaterial range • Exposure to organic solvents, corrosive chemicals and PHS • Chemical and thermal burn • Electrical shock during maintenance and other activities involving opening the machine • Potential for fire/explosion due to flammable solvents, combustible dust (in powder printing) and electrical/printer malfunction etc.

answer: Working in research laboratories can have potential for exposure to reproductive hazards. Reproductive hazards are substances or agents that may affect the reproductive health of women or men or the ability to have healthy children. The “Health Hazard” pictogram on the GHS- compliant chemical label is an initial indication of the possibility of a chemical being a reproductive toxin. The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) Section 2 can provide further details such as standardized Hazard Statements (e.g., “May Cause harm to breast-fed children”, “May damage fertility or the unborn child”, etc.). You can also contact your safety specialist for assistance. OMS may be consulted by all staff of reproductive capability (i.e., women, men, women who are pregnant, women who may soon become pregnant, women who are breastfeeding) when there is a concern for past exposure or potential future exposure to reproductive hazard(s).

question: Reproductive Toxins相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Reproductive toxins are agents that may affect reproductive capabilities including chromosomal damage (mutagens) and produce effects on developing fetuses (teratogens). Reproductive toxins can affect both men and women. Examples of adverse reproductive health effects include birth defects, spontaneous abortion, fetal developmental damage, and infertility. It is important to note that the first trimester of pregnancy is the period of most concern to the developing fetus because this is when the organs and the limbs are being formed. During this period, many women may not yet be aware that they are pregnant. For this reason, it is important that the use of reproductive toxins have been identified and that control measures are in place to protect a woman and her fetus from harmful exposure levels.

answer: Flammables (including flammable liquids and solids) are substances that can ignite and burn readily (e.g. ethanol, diethyl ether, 2-propanol etc.). Always keep flammables stored inside an approved flammable cabinet and away from oxidizers, corrosives, heat or ignition sources (e.g., radiators, electric power panels, etc.). The maximum allowed quantity of flammable and combustible liquids stored in a laboratory at NIH is 50 gallons (Class I, II and III combined). No more than 10 gallons (38 L) of Class I flammable liquids (diethyl ether, pentane etc.) can be stored in a laboratory. Limit flammables and combustibles outside of flammable cabinets to what is actively in use. No more than 10 gallons (38L) of flammable liquids of any class are allowed outside of flammable cabinets.

Introduction A cryogen, or cryogenic liquid, is any liquid with a boiling point below 93K (-180°C or -240°F) at 1 atmosphere of pressure. The most common cryogens used in research laboratories are Liquid nitrogen (LN2), liquid helium (LHe), and occasionally liquid oxygen (LO2). Cryogenic liquids rapidly freeze human tissue, and they cause many common materials to crack or fracture under stress. All cryogenic liquids vaporize, generating large amounts of gases and may create an oxygen-deficient atmosphere. Toxicity is another hazard for cryogenic liquids like carbon monoxide, which can release large quantities of highly toxic carbon monoxide gas into the air. Cryogenic liquids with a boiling point below liquid oxygen can condense oxygen from the atmosphere.

answer: DS Fact Sheet on Compatible Chemical Storage National Institutes of Health (NIH) • Office of Research Services (ORS) • Division of Safety (DS) Chemical Storage Chemicals should be separated by hazard class and stored in appropriate chemical storage cabinets. Consult NIH Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) and NIH Chemical Safety Guide. Secondary containment should be used for all hazardous liquids to avoid accidental mixing of incompatible chemicals. Secondary containment must have sufficient capacity to contain 10% of the volume of containers or the volume of the largest container stored within, whichever is greater. All secondary containers should be made of Nalgene trays or an equivalent non-reactive plastic such as polypropylene or polyethylene. Chemicals should never be alphabetized until they are segregated by hazard class first. For all chemicals, please refer to the manufacturer’s Safety Data Sheet (SDS) (Section 7: Handling and Storage, Section 10: Stability and Reactivity) for specific storage requirements.

question: Establishment of Regulated Areas相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: A Regulated area is defined as any area where airborne concentrations of methylene chloride exceed either the 8-hour Time Weighted Average (TWA) permissible exposure limit (PEL) or the Short-Term Exposure Limit (STEL). Within 3 months of receiving the initial monitoring data, areas where airborne concentrations of DCM exceed, or anticipated to exceed the inhalation exposure limits must be marked and isolated as regulated areas. Appropriate signage should mark the area to warn potentially exposed employees about the exposure zone and keep unauthorized individuals entering the regulated area. The sign must have wordings “Danger: Regulated Area. Methylene chloride, authorized personnel only. Respiratory protection and PPE required”. Access to the regulated areas must be limited to only the individuals with proper training and PPE.

We wish to emphasize that the sixth edition of BMBL remains an advisory document recommending best practices for the safe conduct of work in biomedical and clinical laboratories from a biosafety perspective. The BMBL is not intended to be a regulatory document although we recognize that some may use it in that way. The core principle of this document is protocol-driven risk assessment; it is not possible for a single document to identify all of the possible combinations of risks and mitigations feasible in biomedical and clinical labora- tories. For these reasons, organizations and laboratory directors are compelled to evaluate and ensure the effectiveness of their biosafety programs, the proficiency of their workers, as well as the capability of equipment, facilities, and management practices to provide containment and security of microbiological agents. Risk assessment requires careful judgment and is an important responsibility for directors and principal investigators (PI) of micro- biological and biomedical laboratories. Institutional leadership and oversight resources, such as Institutional Biosafety Committees (IBCs) or equivalent resources, animal care and use committees, biological safety professionals, occupational health staff, and laboratory animal veterinarians also share in this responsibility. question: Biosecurity and Select Agent issues are covered in detail in Section VI and相关的实验室安全要求是什么？

answer: When performing experimentation in the laboratory, in addition to the proper laboratory attire and a task appropriate laboratory coat, a risk assessment should be used to determine appropriate hand protection, and eye and face protection devices. Task appropriate hand protection is required when performing laboratory operations and the selection is determined by the laboratory supervisor in accordance with the appropriate standard (ANSI/ISEA 105-2011 for laboratory gloves). Eye protection is mandatory when there is a potential for injury. Eye protection (protective glasses, goggles, faceshield) must be appropriate for the type of hazard (chemical splash or vapors, lasers, ultra violet light) and should be selected by the laboratory supervisor in accordance with the appropriate standard (ANSI/ISEA Z78.1-2015 for safety eyewear). More information on hand and eye protection can be found in section IX of the NIH Chemical Hygiene Plan. Any employee needing prescription safety glasses should consult the Safety Glasses Request section of the Occupational Medical Service website. It is important to ensure that safety eyewear selected for use in laboratories where lasers are present is appropriate for the wavelength of the specific laser used.

question: 2.A.1. Environmental Health and Safety Policy相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Top management should set in place procedures to define, document, and endorse a formal EHS policy for an organization. The policy should clearly outline the roles and expectations for the organization, faculty, EHS personnel, and individual employees or students. It should be developed in communication with laboratory personnel to ensure that all major concerns are adequately addressed. The EHS policy should state intent to prevent or mitigate both human and economic losses arising from accidents, adverse occupational exposures, and environmental events; build EHS considerations into all phases of the operations, including laboratory discovery and development environments; achieve and maintain compliance with laws and regulations; and continually improve EHS performance. The EHS policy and policy statement should be reviewed, revalidated, and where necessary, revised by top management as often as necessary. It should be communicated and made readily accessible to all employees and made available to relevant interested parties, as appropriate.

answer: Top management should review the organization's EHS management system at regular intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. This review includes assessing opportunities for improvement and the need for changes in the management system, including the EHS policy and objectives. The results of the management review should be documented. Among other information, a management review should include the following: results of EHS management system audits, results from any external audits, communications from interested parties, extent to which objectives have been met, status of corrective and preventive actions, follow-up actions from previous management reviews, and recommendations for improvement based on changing circumstances. The outputs from management review should include any decisions and actions related to possible change to EHS policy, objectives, and other elements of the management system, consistent with the commitment to continual improvement. The management system review ensures a regular process that evaluates the EHS management system in order to identify deficiencies and modify them. Systemic gaps, evidence that targets are not being met, or compliance issues that are discovered during compliance or risk assessments indicate a possible need for revision to the management system or its implementation.

The principles and functions in DOE Policy DOE P 450.4 ( DOE, 1994 ), outlined below, require planning, identification of hazards and controls before work begins, and for work to be performed within these defined and planned methods. Principles: Line management responsibility for safety. Line management is directly responsible for the protection of the public, the workers, and the environment. Thus it is imperative that, whenever working in the laboratory, others are actively aware of your activities. answer: Many chemicals and solutions routinely used in laboratories present a significant health risk when handled improperly. The Swiss physician and alchemist Theophrastus Phillippus Aureolus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493-1541), who took the name Paracelsus later in life in homage to Celsus, a Roman physician, is known as “the father of toxicology.” Paracelsus is famous for his quote, “What is it that is not poison? All things are poison and nothing is without poison. It is the dose alone that makes a thing not a poison” ( Dillon, 1994 ). Today, in that same spirit, trained laboratory personnel are encouraged to reduce personal risk by minimizing exposure to hazardous chemicals and by eliminating unsafe work practices in the laboratory. The OSHA Laboratory Standard defines a hazardous chemical as one “for which there is statistically significant evidence based on at least one study conducted in accordance with established scientific principles that acute or chronic health effects may occur in exposed persons.” Note that this definition is not limited to toxic chemicals and includes corrosives, explosives, and other hazard classes. Routes of exposure to hazardous materials include contact with skin and eyes, inhalation, ingestion, and injection.

question: 2.D.2. Chemical Storage相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: To lessen risk of exposure to hazardous chemicals, trained laboratory personnel should separate and store all chemicals according to hazard category and compatibility. In the event of an accident involving a broken container or a chemical spill, incompatible chemicals that are stored in close proximity can mix to produce fires, hazardous fumes, and explosions. Laboratory personnel should read the MSDS and heed the precautions regarding the storage requirements of the chemicals in the laboratory. A detailed chemical compatibility table is included in Chapter 5 , section 5.E.2 , Table 5.1 To avoid accidents, all chemical containers must be properly labeled with the full chemical name, not abbreviations, and using a permanent marker. All transfer vessels should have the following label information: chemical name, hazard warnings, name of manufacturer, name of researcher in charge, and date of transfer to the vessel. Incoming chemical shipments should be dated promptly upon receipt, and chemical stock should be rotated to ensure use of older chemicals. It is good practice to date peroxide formers upon receipt and date again when the container is opened so that the user can dispose of the material according to the recommendations on the MSDS.

question: 2.D.5. Transporting, Transferring, and Shipping Chemicals相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: It is prudent practice to use a secondary containment device (i.e., rubber pail) when transporting chemicals from the storeroom to the laboratory or even short distances within the laboratory. When transporting several containers, use carts with attached side rails and trays of single piece construction at least 2 in. deep to contain a spill that may occur. Bottles of liquids should be separated to avoid breakage and spills. Avoid high-traffic areas when moving chemicals within the building. When possible, use freight elevators when transporting chemicals and do not allow other passengers. If you must use a general traffic elevator, ask other passengers to wait until you have delivered the chemicals.

question: 2.E.1. Types of Inspection Programs: Who Conducts Them and What They Offer相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: There are several types of inspection programs, each providing a different perspective and function. A comprehensive laboratory inspection program includes a combination of some or all of these programs. Routine Inspections Trained laboratory personnel and supervisors should complete general equipment and facility inspections on a regular basis. Consult the label and the MSDS prior to the initial use of each hazardous substance. Always use the minimal amount of the chemical and use caution when transporting the chemical. Most laboratory workers should be able to clean up incidental spills of the materials they use. Lab workers should be instructed to contact EHS personnel to evaluate how to proceed with spill cleanup.

question: 2.G. EMPLOYEE SAFETY TRAINING PROGRAM相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Newly hired employees or students working in a laboratory should be required to attend basic safety training prior to their first day. Additional training should be provided to laboratory personnel as they advance in their laboratory duties or when they are required to handle a chemical or use equipment for the first time. The organization should provide ongoing safety activities that serve to promote a culture of safety in the workplace that will begin when the person begins work and will continue for the length of their tenure. question: 1.B. THE CULTURE OF LABORATORY SAFETY相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: As a result of the promulgation of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Laboratory Standard (29 CFR § 1910.1450), a culture of safety consciousness, accountability, organization, and education has developed in industrial, governmental, and academic laboratories. Safety and training programs, often coordinated through an office of environment, health, and safety (EHS), have been implemented to monitor the handling of chemicals from the moment they are ordered until their departure for ultimate disposal and to train laboratory personnel in safe practices. 1 Laboratory personnel realize that the welfare and safety of each individual depends on clearly defined attitudes of teamwork and personal responsibility and that laboratory safety is not simply a matter of materials and equipment but also of processes and behaviors. Learning to participate in this culture of habitual risk assessment, experiment planning, and consideration of worst-case possibilities—for oneself and one's fellow workers—is as much part of a scientific education as learning the theoretical background of experiments or the step-by-step protocols for doing them in a professional manner. 2 Accordingly, a crucial component of chemical education at every level is to nurture basic attitudes and habits of prudent behavior so that safety is a valued and inseparable part of all laboratory activities.

answer: Ensuring a safe laboratory environment is the combined responsibility of laboratory personnel, EHS personnel, and the management of an organization, though the primary responsibility lies with the individual performing the work. Of course, federal, state, and local laws and regulations make safety in the laboratory a legal requirement and an economic necessity. Laboratory safety, although altruistic, is not a purely voluntary function; it requires mandatory safety rules and programs and an ongoing commitment to them. A sound safety organization that is respected by all requires the participation and support of laboratory administrators, employees, and students. The ultimate responsibility for creating a safe environment and for encouraging a culture of safety rests with the head of the organization and its operating units. Leadership by those in charge ensures that an effective safety program is embraced by all. Even a well-conceived safety program will be treated casually by workers if it is neglected by top management.

question: 1.F.1. Advances in Technology相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: In response to the increasingly high cost of chemical management, from procurement to waste disposal, a steady movement toward miniaturizing chemical operations exists in both teaching and research laboratories. This trend has had a significant effect on laboratory design and has also reduced the costs associated with procurement, handling, and disposal of chemicals. Another trend—motivated at least partially by safety concerns—is the simulation of laboratory experiments by computer. Such programs are a valuable conceptual adjunct to laboratory training but are by no means a substitute for hands-on experimental work. Only students who have been carefully educated through a series of hands-on experiments in the laboratory have the confidence and expertise needed to handle real laboratory procedures safely as they move on to advanced courses, research work, and eventually to their careers in industry, academe, health sciences, or government laboratories. Environmental Impact If a laboratory operation produces less waste, there is less waste to dispose of and less impact on the environment. A frequent, but not universal, corollary is that costs are also reduced.

answer: Perhaps the most significant impediment to comprehensive waste reduction in laboratories is the element of scale. Techniques that are practical and cost-effective on a 55-gal or tank-car quantity of material may be highly unrealistic when applied to a 50-g (or milligram) quantity, or vice versa. Evaluating the costs of both equipment and time becomes especially important when dealing with very small quantities. Changes in the Legal and Regulatory Requirements Changes in the legal and regulatory requirements over the past several decades have greatly affected laboratory operations. Because of increased regulations, the collection and disposal of laboratory waste constitute major budget items in the operation of every chemical laboratory. The cost of accidents in terms of time and money spent on fines for regulatory violations and on litigation are significant. Of course, protection of students and research personnel from toxic materials is not only an economic necessity but an ethical obligation.

As part of that culture, all levels of the organization (i.e., administrative personnel, scientists, laboratory technicians) should understand the importance of minimizing the risk of exposure to hazardous materials in the laboratory and should work together toward this end. question: 7.B. WORKING WITH WATER-COOLED EQUIPMENT相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: The use of water as a coolant in laboratory condensers and other equipment is common practice. Although tap water is often used for these purposes, this practice should be discouraged. In many localities conserving water is essential and makes tap water inappropriate. In addition, the potential for a flood is greatly increased. Refrigerated recirculators can be expensive, but are preferred for cooling laboratory equipment to conserve water and to minimize the impact of floods. To prevent freezing at the refrigeration coils, using a mixture of water and ethylene glycol as the coolant is prudent. Spills of this mixture are very slippery and must be cleaned thoroughly to prevent slips and falls.

answer: Electric shock is the major electrical hazard. Although relatively low current of 10 mA poses some danger, 80 to 100 mA can be fatal. In addition, if improperly used, electrical equipment can ignite flammable or explosive vapors. Most of the risks can be minimized by regular proper maintenance and a clear understanding of the correct use of the device. answer: Many laboratory locations are classified under fire and electrical codes with a mandate for nonsparking explosion-proof motors and electrical equipment. Areas where large amounts of flammable solvents are in use also require explosion-proof lighting and electrical fixtures. The owners of such facilities are responsible for ensuring that all electrical equipment and fixtures meet these codes and regulations. Equip motor-driven electrical equipment used in a laboratory where volatile flammable materials may be present with either nonsparking induction motors that meet Class 1, Division 2, Group C-D electrical standards ( Earley, 2008 ; NFPA, 2008 ) or air motors instead of series-wound motors that use carbon brushes, such as those generally used in vacuum pumps, mechanical shakers, stirring motors, magnetic stirrers, and rotary evaporators. Do not use variable autotransformers to control the speed of an induction motor. The speed of an induction motor is determined by the AC frequency rather than the voltage. Thus, using a variable autotransformer that controls voltage and not frequency could cause the motor to overheat and presents a fire hazard.

question: 7.C.3. Refrigerators and Freezers相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: The potential hazards posed by laboratory refrigerators include release of vapors from the contents, the possible presence of incompatible chemicals, and spillage. As general precautions, laboratory refrigerators should be placed against fire-resistant walls, should have heavy-duty power cords, and preferably should be protected by their own circuit breaker. Enclose the contents of a laboratory refrigerator in unbreakable secondary containment. Because there is almost never a satisfactory way to continuously vent the interior atmosphere of a refrigerator, any vapors escaping from vessels placed in one will accumulate in the refrigerated space and gradually be absorbed into the surrounding insulation. Thus, the atmosphere in a refrigerator could contain an explosive mixture of air and the vapor of a flammable substance or a dangerously high concentration of the vapor of a toxic substance or both. The impact of exposure to toxic substances can be aggravated when a person inserts his or her head inside a refrigerator to search for a particular sample. Placing potentially explosive (see Chapter 6 , sections 6.C and 6.G ) or highly toxic substances (see Chapter 6 , sections 6.D and 6.E ) in a laboratory refrigerator is strongly discouraged.

Never carry out reactions in, or apply heat to, an apparatus that is a closed system unless it has been designed and tested to withstand pressure. To ensure that the equipment has been properly designed, each pressure vessel should have stamped on it, or on an attached plate, its maximum allowable working pressure, the allowable temperature at this pressure, and the material of construction. Similarly, the relief pressure—the pressure at which the safety system (e.g., rupture disk or safety vent) will be triggered—and setting data should be stamped on a metal tag attached to installed pressure-relief devices, and the setting mechanisms should be sealed. answer: Do not allow unprotected parts of the body to come in contact with uninsulated vessels or pipes that contain cryogenic liquids because extremely cold material may bond firmly to the skin and tear flesh if separation or withdrawal is attempted. Even very brief skin contact with a cryogenic liquid can cause tissue damage similar to that of frostbite or thermal burns, and prolonged contact may result in blood clots that have potentially very serious consequences. Gloves must be insulated, impervious to the fluid being handled, and loose enough to be tossed off easily in case the cryogenic liquid becomes trapped close to the skin. Never wear tight gloves when working with cryogenic liquids. Trained laboratory personnel are also encouraged to wear long sleeves when handling cryogenic fluids. Handle objects that are in contact with cryogenic liquids with tongs or potholders. Virtually all liquid gases present the threat of poisoning, explosion, or, at a minimum, asphyxiation in a confined space.

answer: Selection of Low-Temperature Equipment Select equipment used at low temperatures carefully because temperature can dramatically change characteristics of materials. For example, the impact strength of ordinary carbon steel is greatly reduced at low temperatures, and failure can occur at points of weakness, such as notches or abrupt changes in the material of construction. When combinations of materials are required, consider the temperature dependence of their volumes so that leaks, ruptures, and glass fractures are avoided. For example, O-rings that provide a good seal at room temperature may lose resilience and fail to function on chilled equipment. Stainless steels containing 18% chromium and 8% nickel retain their impact resistance down to approximately −240 °C; the exact value depends heavily on special design considerations. The impact resistance of aluminum, copper, nickel, and many other nonferrous metals and alloys increases with decreasing temperatures. Use special alloy steels for liquids or gases containing hydrogen at temperatures greater than 200 °C or at pressures greater than 34.5 MPa (500 psi) because of the danger of weakening carbon steel equipment by hydrogen embrittlement.

answer: Vacuum work can result in an implosion and the possible hazards of flying glass, spattering chemicals, and fire. Set up and operate all vacuum operations with careful consideration of the potential risks. Although a vacuum distillation apparatus may appear to provide some of its own protection in the form of heating mantles and column insulation, this is not sufficient because an implosion could scatter hot flammable liquid. Use an explosion shield and a full-face shield to protect laboratory personnel, and carry the procedure out in a laboratory chemical hood. Glassware under vacuum should be kept behind a shield or hood sash, taped, or resin (plastic) coated. Equipment at reduced pressure is especially prone to rapid pressure changes, which can create large pressure differences within the apparatus. Shield them, either by a layer of fiber-reinforced friction tape or by enclosure in a wooden or metal container, to reduce the risk of flying glass in case of collapse. Use metal Dewar flasks whenever there is a possibility of breakage. Styrofoam buckets with lids can be a safer form of short-term storage and conveyance of cryogenic liquids than glass vacuum Dewar flasks. Although they do not insulate as well as Dewar flasks, they eliminate the danger of implosion. answer: Eye and Face Protection Appropriate eye protection is a requirement for working in a chemical laboratory. Requisite eye protection should be provided for laboratory personnel and visitors, and signs should be posted outside the laboratory indicating that eye protection is required where hazardous chemicals are in use. Ordinary prescription glasses with hardened lenses do not serve as eye protection in the laboratory. Appropriate laboratory eye and face protection includes impact goggles with splash protection (chemical splash goggles), full-face shields that also protect the throat, and specialized eye protection (i.e., protection against ultraviolet light or laser light). The following provides basic information regarding eye protection. (For more information, see Chapter 6 , section 6.C.2.2 .) Wear impact protection goggles if there is a danger of flying particles, and full-face shields with safety glasses and side shields for complete face and throat protection. Although safety glasses can provide satisfactory protection from flying particles, they do not fit tightly against the face and offer little protection against splashes or sprays of chemicals.

A fixed shield that completely surrounds the experimental apparatus can afford protection against minor blast damage. Polymethyl methacrylate, polycarbonate, poly(vinyl chloride), and laminated safety plate glass are all satisfactory transparent shielding materials. Where combustion is possible, the shielding material should be nonflammable or slow burning; if it can withstand the working blast pressure, laminated safety plate glass may be the best material for such circumstances. question: Each area where respirators are used should have written information available t（续）相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Respirators for routine use should be inspected before each use by the user and periodically by the laboratory supervisor. Self-contained breathing apparatus should be inspected at least once a month and cleaned after each use. Safety Showers and Eyewash Units Make safety showers available in areas where chemicals are handled; make sure they meet all installation and maintenance requirements (ANSI Z358.1 Emergency Eyewash and Shower Equipment; ANSI, 2004 ). Use them for immediate first-aid treatment of chemical splashes and for extinguishing clothing fires. All trained laboratory personnel should know where the safety showers are located in the work area and should learn how to use them. Test safety showers routinely to ensure that the valve is operable and to remove any debris in the system. The shower should drench the subject immediately and be large enough to accommodate more than one person if necessary.

question: 7.G. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: The following general emergency procedures are recommended in the event of a fire, explosion, spill, or medical or other laboratory accident. These procedures are intended to limit injuries and minimize damage if an accident should occur. Post numbers to call in emergencies clearly at all telephones in hazard areas. Because emergency response (personnel, contact information, procedures) varies greatly from institution to institution, all laboratory personnel should be properly trained and informed of the protocols for their particular institution. Have someone call for emergency help, for instance, 911 or other number as designated by the institution. State clearly where the accident has occurred and its nature. Ascertain the safety of the situation.

answer: If a chemical has splashed into the eye, immediately wash the eyeball and the inner surface of the eyelid with water for 15 minutes. An eyewash unit should be used if available. Forcibly hold the eye open to wash thoroughly behind the eyelid. If possible, determine the identity of the chemical and inform the emergency medical personnel attending the injured person. answer: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulation 29 CFR 1910.1450, Occupational Exposure to Hazardous Chemicals in Laboratories , requires employers to develop and implement a Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) that protects laboratory personnel from chemical health and safety hazards and ensures exposures remain below applicable OSHA Permissible Exposure Limits (PELs). This document constitutes the official Cornell University Chemical Hygiene Plan. Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) maintains the institutional CHP and provides program oversight, technical guidance, and supporting resources. The CHP establishes the minimum safety requirements for the use, handling, and management of hazardous chemicals in all Cornell research and teaching laboratories. Laboratories and departments may develop additional manuals, procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to address local hazards or specialized operations. These documents must supplement—and cannot replace or reduce—the requirements of the Cornell University Chemical Hygiene Plan.

answer: Certain laboratory operations involve elevated risks due to the chemical, physical, or procedural hazards involved. Examples include work with pyrophoric or water-reactive materials, hydrofluoric acid, acutely toxic gases, highly reactive chemicals, peroxide-forming compounds, or processes involving significant heat, pressure, or scale-up. These activities may require additional review before work begins to ensure appropriate controls are in place. Because research practices vary widely across the University, a single institution-wide prior approval process is not feasible. Instead, Principal Investigators and laboratory supervisors are responsible for identifying high-hazard operations in their laboratories and ensuring that appropriate review and control measures are documented in laboratory SOPs or other internal procedures. EHS is available to assist in identifying high-hazard conditions, reviewing associated controls, and providing guidance on work involving particularly hazardous substances (PHS), such as select carcinogens, reproductive toxins, and acute toxins. Additional resources, including SDSs and reference materials such as Prudent Practices in the Laboratory and Safety in Academic Chemistry Laboratories , may also inform laboratory-specific review processes.

Principal Investigators and laboratory supervisors are responsible for identifying PHS and other high-hazard operations in their laboratories and ensuring that appropriate controls are implemented and documented in laboratory SOPs and training. EHS is available to assist in evaluating hazards and recommending additional safeguards to protect laboratory personnel. Additional protective measures may include: establishing designated areas for PHS or high-hazard chemical use, using containment devices such as fume hoods, gloveboxes, or other appropriate engineering controls, implementing procedures for the safe handling, storage, and removal of contaminated materials and waste, enhanced decontamination procedures for work surfaces and equipment, and incorporating these requirements into laboratory-specific SOPs, hazard assessments, and training. question: 7.1.5 Hydrofluoric Acid相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Hydrofluoric acid is a strong corrosive and highly toxic chemical that causes severe burns from dilute solutions and can be fatal upon exposure of concentrated solutions. Bench top use of hydrofluoric acid is not permitted; it must only be used in a fume hood. Anyone using Hydrofluoric acid must contact the Gannett Health Center and purchase a tube of Calcium gluconate gel, which is used as an initial response to skin exposure of Hydrofluoric acid. The quantities of Hydrofluoric acid that are used and stored should be kept to an absolute minimum. All users of hydrofluoric acid must attend hydrofluoric acid training. More information on hydrofluoric acid can be found in the Laboratory Safety Manual and Chemical Hygiene Plan. Due to the toxic nature, do not attempt to neutralize hydrofluoric acid - dispose of hydrofluoric acid waste through the hazardous waste management program .

question: 7.5 Asbestos相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Asbestos is a fibrous material that was once widely used in a number of products that can still be found in laboratories and throughout other buildings. Products that can contain asbestos include: electrical equipment insulation (ovens, heating mantles, heating pads, and wires), older vinyl floor tiles and mastic, pipe fittings, pipe insulation, caulking compounds, fireproofing, and transite (cement-like) panels such as those found in and under fume hoods. Asbestos is a known human carcinogen and must be disposed of properly. The hazard of asbestos is greatest when the asbestos product becomes “friable” – able to be pulverized from finger pressure – and when the asbestos becomes airborne. For older vinyl asbestos tile (VAT), an additional slipping hazard occurs when these tiles “pop” out of the floor. If you find any of the above items deteriorating and suspect they may contain asbestos, or you are considering disposing of old electrical equipment with insulation, or if vinyl tiles have “popped” out of the floor, then please contact the asbestos coordinator at 607-254-5439 for more information.

question: 7.15 Reactive and Potentially Explosive Chemicals相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Reactive chemicals such as strong oxidizers and reducers, and air/water reactive chemicals must be disposed of through the hazardous waste management program. Because of their reactive nature, it is important to minimize the quantity of reactive chemicals in storage. If the integrity of the container appears to be compromised, then dispose of the chemicals as hazardous waste promptly. Never dispose of reactive chemicals, such as Sodium metal, regardless of the quantity, down the drain or in the normal trash. Such practices can result in fires, toxic vapors and gases being released, and injury to people. When disposing of these compounds, please note any special hazards on the Hazardous Waste Label . Some of these compounds can become unstable and potentially explosive over time due to contamination with air, water, other material, or when the chemical dries out.

answer: Safe management of ethidium bromide (EtBr) involves both prevention of exposure and proper handling of waste. Because EtBr is a potent mutagen, waste solutions, gels, and contaminated surfaces must be treated as hazardous chemical waste. Modern best practice focuses on adsorption and controlled collection rather than bleach oxidation, which is no longer recommended due to incomplete destruction and formation of chlorinated byproducts. Activated Charcoal Adsorption Aqueous EtBr solutions can be treated using activated charcoal filters, columns, or commercial "tea bag" kits . These methods remove EtBr by adsorption. After treatment, the filtrate may be checked under UV light to confirm the absence of orange fluorescence. If no fluorescence is observed, and if permitted by institutional policy, the filtrate may be disposed of via the sanitary drain.

title: Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - There are some easy ways to preventing the generation of unknown chemicals/materials:

question: There are some easy ways to preventing the generation of unknown chemicals/materials:相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Ensure that a label is present on all containers of chemicals including containers of wastes. This means all containers even beakers, test tubes, wash bottles and other containers. Use chemical names to identify the contents of containers. For hazardous wastes generated at Cornell this is a requirement. Do not use formulas, abbreviations or chemical structures on waste labels. Containers in which the labels are degrading or falling off should be given a new label immediately. Check laboratory notebooks for information related to vials or test tubes.

question: 1.5.2.1 Container Labeling相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: All containers of hazardous chemicals must be labeled identifying their contents. Labels on hazardous chemicals must not be removed or defaced except when empty. Chemical labels on purchased chemicals are required to provide you with safety information to help you protect yourself while working with this substance. This includes physical and health hazard warnings, protective measures for handling the material, first-aid instructions, storage information, and procedures to follow in the event of a fire, leak, or spill. All labels on chemicals purchased after June 2015 must include the information required by the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard. Manufacturers and importers of these chemicals must provide a label that includes a signal word (Danger, Warning), pictogram(s), hazard statement(s), and precautionary statement(s) based on the hazard classification and category of the chemical. This requirement ensures consistent, uniform hazard information across all chemical containers, regardless of manufacturer or supplier.

answer: 2.3.1 Standard Laboratory Clothing – Appropriate Attire Even when there is no immediate risk of skin contact with a hazardous chemical, it is still important to wear clothing that minimizes exposed skin when in the laboratory. Laboratory Personnel must wear safety or prescription glasses, pants or clothing that covers the legs (shorts and short skirts are not acceptable), and closed- toe, solid-top shoes in the laboratory at all times. Safety glasses, exam-style gloves, and a laboratory coat (or its equivalent in certain circumstances – apron, barrier gown, etc.) are required to be worn whenever working with hazardous materials. Prescription glasses may be worn only when working with hazardous materials if they are prescription safety glasses with side shields. question: 2.3.3 Gloves相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Chemical-resistant gloves must be worn whenever handling hazardous chemicals or whenever there is a possibility of contact with hazardous materials. Gloves should be selected based on the materials being handled, the specific hazard involved, and the operation's requirements. Before each use, gloves should be checked for integrity. Exam-style gloves are most commonly used for laboratory work and are disposed of in the regular trash after each use. In general, nitrile exam-style gloves provide better chemical protection than latex or vinyl gloves. All laboratories that use chemicals should stock and use nitrile gloves. Latex gloves are discouraged not only because they do not hold up well to many chemicals, but also because of the potential for the user or other lab personnel to develop a sensitization to the latex.

question: 2.3.4 Eye Protection相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Eye protection is required for all people present in laboratories where hazardous materials are handled or stored. Prescription eyeglasses may be worn in lieu of safety glasses if not handling hazardous materials in the laboratory, however safety glasses with side shields must be worn when handling hazardous materials. Safety glasses, goggles, and goggles with a face shield should be worn in the laboratory based upon the physical state, the volume, the operation, or the level of toxicity of the chemicals used. Goggles should be worn in situations where bulk quantities of chemicals are handled and chemical splashes to the eyes are possible. Goggles form a liquid-proof seal around the eyes, protecting them from splashes. When handling highly reactive substances, chemicals under pressure, or larger quantities of corrosives, poisons, and hot chemicals, goggles with face shield should be worn.

question: Report an Incident (SU-17)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Health & Safety Topics Standard Operating Procedures Biohazardous waste includes all laboratory waste that may contain any biohazardous material or were in contact with said material. Additionally, any blood or components of blood or body fluids are to be disposed of as biohazardous waste, as are human or non-human primate cell lines. All biohazardous waste must be disposed of in red bags marked with the biohazard symbol; these bags must be secondarily contained in a puncture resistant outer container and covered with a tight fitting lid. Biohazard stickers must be present on all four sides of the container and the top of the lid. In accordance with the California Medical Waste Management Act, Health and Safety Code, Chapter 6.1, medical waste is defined as including, but not limited to the following: Human or animal specimens or cultures from medical and pathological laboratories. question: Manage chemical waste safely相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: University personnel who generate hazardous chemical waste at the University (including all campuses and off-site locations) are required to follow chemical waste management practices. Refer to the UW Laboratory Safety Manual for additional information. EH&S recommends hazardous chemical waste generators use the Hazardous Waste Checklist as a self-audit tool to verify compliance with waste accumulation rules and prepare for periodic hazardous waste inspections by the Washington State Department of Ecology. Chemical waste basics What is “hazardous chemical waste”? Hazardous chemical waste is defined as any liquid, gaseous, or solid chemical that is ignitable, corrosive, reactive, toxic, or persistent, and is no longer useful or wanted. Some additional chemicals are managed as hazardous waste at UW because they are known, probable or suspected carcinogens, teratogens, irritants and/or sensitizers (refer to a chemical’s safety data sheet to determine if the chemical is any of these.) Mixtures of chemicals may not be hazardous waste, depending on their concentration and toxicity. Refer to Section 3 of the Laboratory Safety Manual for information on how to calculate whether a mixture of chemicals is hazardous waste.

answer: Why do I need to submit a Chemical Waste Collection Request before EH&S picks up my chemical waste? EH&S needs the information you provide in the Chemical Waste Collection Request for safety, legal, and logistical reasons. Safety: Knowing the potential hazards associated with each container allows EH&S staff to prepare for safely evaluating, handling, transporting, and storing chemicals prior to disposal. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Department of Transportation, and Washington State Department of Ecology regulations require us to accurately designate the contents of each container so it can be transported legally and disposed of properly by applying the correct hazardous waste codes and treatment standards. Logistical: We need to know in advance what’s inside the containers to be sure we don’t pick up anything that can’t be transported or disposed of. We also need to know how many containers there are, and the type(s) and size(s) of containers to ensure we have the correct number of transport tubs and space in the vehicle.

answer: Treatment and Recycling Notice of Cleaning and Decontamination Fume hoods are a primary method of exposure control in the laboratory. A fume hood is a ventilated enclosure that usually vents separately from the building’s heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system and not recirculated into the building. Fume hoods should be used when working with toxic compounds or compounds with a boiling point below 120°C. Fume hoods, or other effective local ventilation, must be provided and used when the materials used will exceed exposure limits in the laboratory.

question: Constant air volume hoods相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: The constant air volume (CAV) fume hood exhausts the same amount of air all the time, regardless of sash position. As the sash is lowered and raised, the velocity at the face of the hood changes. EH&S tests all hoods regularly and marks the opening that gives the correct face velocity (see image at left) on constant air volume hoods. Variable air volume hoods Some newer models, called variable air volume (VAV) hoods, modulate air flow based on sash height and maintain 100 feet per minute face velocity at all sash heights. EH&S tests VAV hoods, but does not mark the sash height since it's always 100 feet per minute. VAV fume hoods are equipped with a monitor (see image at right) that indicates whether the hood is in "standard operation" or "standby operation" mode. The fume hood monitor also has an "emergency purge" button, which increases airflow through the hood to maximum and can be used to quickly remove air contaminates from the lab.

question: Select compatible containers相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Chemical compatibility: Choose a container chemically compatible with the material it will hold. Chemicals must not react with, weaken, or dissolve the container or lid. Follow these basic compatibility guidelines: Acids or bases: Do not store in metal. Hydrofluoric acid: Do not store in glass. Gasoline (solvents): Do not store or transport in lightweight polyethylene containers such as milk jugs. Read Chemical Compatibility Guidelines for more detailed information. Use waste containers with leak-proof, screw-on caps so contents can't leak if a container tips over.

question: I. Identifying Regulated Chemical Wastes相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: A regulated chemical waste is defined as a waste which, due to its quantity, concentration, or physical and chemical characteristics may: cause, or significantly contribute to, an increase in mortality or an increase in serious or incapacitating illness; or pose a substantial present or potential threat to human health or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, disposed of, or otherwise managed. Characteristics of Chemical Wastes In the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) defines the four fundamental characteristics of regulated waste as: 1. Ignitability - Ignitable materials are defined as materials exhibiting one or more of the following characteristics: Liquids that have a flash point less than 60°C (140°F). Materials other than liquids that are capable, under standard temperature and pressure, of causing fire by friction, adsorption of moisture, or spontaneous chemical changes and, when ignited, burn so vigorously and persistently that they create a hazard. Flammable compressed gases, including those that form flammable mixtures with air. Oxidizers that stimulate combustion of organic materials. Corrosivity - Corrosive materials are defined as materials meeting one or more of the following criteria: Aqueous solutions with a pH of less than or equal to 2 or greater than or equal to 12.5.

If you have an unknown chemical waste that needs to be removed you should: Try to identify the contents by asking other researchers, shop personnel, building manager or users in your work area if they know who produced the waste If you cannot find the original generator, attempt to narrow down the potential sources of generation If you have exhausted all available information and still cannot identify the waste you may submit as an “Unknown.” EHS – HMM will inspect and analyze the material. Generators of unknown wastes MAY BE responsible for the costs associated with analyzing and disposal of unknown wastes. Unknown wastes require special handling procedures and may not be acceptable for standard removal depending on the container’s condition, source, and other factors.

question: F. Peroxide Formers and Other Unstable Chemical Waste相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Disposal and Testing Guidance Older containers of peroxidizable chemicals, or containers of unknown age or history, must be handled very carefully and should never be opened by researchers. Any peroxidizable chemical with visible discoloration, cloudiness, crystallization, wisp-like structures, or oily layer (or other liquid heterogeneity/stratification) should be treated as potentially explosive. Older steel containers that have visible rust may also be extremely dangerous. If any of these conditions are observed on a peroxidizable chemical, or if the origin and age of the container are unknown, do not attempt to move or open the container. If any of such containers are found, please contact EHS – HMM immediately. Testing strips are available from EHS for instances in which laboratories do not have their own peroxide test strips. For peroxides concentrations of < 20 ppm, either neutralize the peroxides in the compounds using an approved method or dispose of the chemical through EHS – HMM and indicate the peroxide level in the notes.

title: NC State Fume Hoods and Lab Exhaust - NC State Fume Hoods and Lab Exhaust - section 1
hazard_types: 通风柜;实验室排风;维护;检查
scenario: 参考NC State Environmental Health and Safety公开资料处理通风柜和实验室排风相关实验室安全问题
question: NC State Fume Hoods and Lab Exhaust - section 1相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
answer: Fume Hoods and Lab Exhaust – Environmental Health and Safety Environmental Health and Safety Find a Subject Matter Expert Environmental Affairs Research and Lab Safety Find Training Courses Personal Protective Equipment – PPE Principal Investigator Resources Safety Orientation Checklist Emergency Management & Mission Continuity Accident Report Forms Fume Hoods and Lab Exhaust Fume hoods are the most important engineering controls for preventing exposure to hazardous materials in laboratories. Users need to understand the proper use and limitations of the fume hood. Each fume hood should be equipped with a flow monitor/ alarm. When the alarm sounds, stop work immediately, close the sash, and report the event to facilities liaison. Local exhaust devices other than fume hoods including snorkels and enclosures are also utilized in laboratories for limited applications. title: 沙浴和油浴比水浴温度更高（可达300°C+），需要注意什么？

scenario: 沙浴和油浴加热的安全使用

title: 使用Schlenk line进行无水无氧操作时需要注意什么？
hazard_types: 无水无氧操作;自燃;爆炸;高压气体
scenario: Schlenk line（双排管）的安全操作
question: Schlenk line是空气敏感化学的核心设备。安全操作极为重要：1) 使用前检查所有接头、橡胶管、玻璃活栓是否完好；2) 确认真空泵油洁净（受污染泵油可能反应爆炸）；3) 惰性气体（N₂/Ar）减压阀设置正确（出口压力0.1-0.3 bar）；4) 切换真空/惰气时缓慢操作玻璃活栓（过猛可能导致玻璃断裂）；5) 冷阱中必须使用液氮（不是干冰），冷阱在Schlenk line与真空泵之间捕获挥发性溶剂；6) 冷阱在停止真空后不可立即取下——必须先释放真空再断开；7) Schlenk line不可用于处理自燃试剂（如叔丁基锂），此类操作须在手套箱中。

title: 使用ICP-OES时需要注意哪些安全事项？

hazard_types: 高温等离子体;有毒气体;高压电;紫外辐射
scenario: ICP-OES的安全操作
question: ICP-OES使用高温等离子体（6000-10000K），安全要求严格：1) 确认排风系统正常（等离子体产生臭氧和NOx需及时排出）；2) 检查蠕动泵管和雾化器状态；3) 氩气纯度≥99.996%且压力正常；4) 进样管和排液管连接正确（废液管必须有U型液封）；5) 点火前确认炬管位置正确且干燥；6) 等离子体运行时不得开炬室门；7) 关机前用去离子水冲洗雾化系统5-10分钟（防止盐结晶）。

steps: 检查排风和氩气→安装进样/排液管→点火→稳定10-15分钟→运行标准曲线→测试样品→冲洗系统→熄火→关闭气源

title: 使用FTIR时需要注意什么？

title: 使用索氏提取器时要注意哪些安全事项？

scenario: 索氏提取器的安全操作
question: 索氏提取器用于固液连续萃取，通常使用有机溶剂，操作时间可长达数小时。安全要求：1) 所有玻璃接口严密配合（使用适量真空脂），防止溶剂蒸气泄漏；2) 冷凝水在加热前开启，确认水流畅通；3) 加热温度控制在溶剂沸点以上10-20°C（使溶剂蒸气能上升但不过快）；4) 提取过程不可无人值守——溶剂蒸干会导致烧瓶干烧破裂；5) 提取结束后先停加热，继续通冷凝水至装置冷却；6) 使用易燃溶剂时（乙醚、石油醚等）水浴加热（不可用电热套）。

title: 使用超声波细胞破碎仪时需要注意什么？

hazard_types: 高强度噪声;气溶胶;样品飞溅;探头过热

title: 手套箱的详细安全操作规程是什么？
hazard_types: 自燃;缺氧;压力;化学品暴露
scenario: 手套箱的详细安全操作规程
question: 手套箱是最复杂的实验室设备之一。详细规程：1) 进出手套箱的物品须通过过渡仓（大仓至少3次抽真空-充惰气循环，小仓至少5次）;2) 禁止带入：水溶液、挥发溶剂、尖锐物品（刺破手套）、含活性氢的溶剂（醇/酸会毒化催化剂）;3) 手套箱内不存放超过日常用量的化学品和溶剂;4) 循环系统定期再生（铜催化剂约每3-6个月再生一次，分子筛约每月）;5) 氧/水含量超标时（H₂O>5ppm或O₂>5ppm），立即停止敏感实验，排查漏点;6) 手套破损须立即停止使用并用胶塞堵住破口，更换手套后重新置换箱内气氛。

title: 使用电化学工作站时需要注意什么？
hazard_types: 触电;化学品泄漏;有毒气体
scenario: 电化学工作站的安全操作
question: 电化学工作站涉及电极、电解液和电位控制。安全要求：1) 使用前检查电极线和工作电极/参比电极/对电极连接正确；2) 电解液不得渗漏到电极夹和仪器接口；3) 电解过程中可能产生气体（如电解水产生H₂和O₂），良好通风防止气体积聚；4) 使用有机电解液时在通风柜内操作（如乙腈+四丁基铵盐体系）；5) 参比电极的填充液定期补充（如Ag/AgCl电极的饱和KCl溶液）。

title: 丁腈手套不能防哪些化学品？使用中有什么限制？
category: 丁腈手套使用限制与注意事项
hazard_types: 化学品渗透;手套降解;过敏
scenario: 丁腈手套的使用限制
question: 丁腈手套是实验室最通用的防化手套，但有重要使用限制。不耐受的化学品包括：二氯甲烷（几分钟渗透）、丙酮（快速渗透）、浓硝酸（氧化降解）、浓硫酸（90%+浓度快速降解）、DMF（可渗透）、乙酸乙酯（渗透较快）。丁腈手套的渗透时间因厚度而异——薄型（2-4 mil）渗透快，厚型（6-8 mil）渗透较慢。使用中一旦感到手套内湿滑或闻到化学品气味，说明已经渗透，应立即脱除更换。对于上述不耐受化学品，需选择层压膜手套（如Silver Shield/4H）或双层手套组合。

title: 什么情况下需要使用层压膜手套？如何使用？
hazard_types: 高毒化学品;强渗透溶剂
scenario: 层压膜手套（Silver Shield/4H）的使用
question: 层压膜手套（如Silver Shield/4H/Beta-Safe等）由多层聚合物薄膜制成，耐化学品渗透性远超普通防化手套。适用于：1) 处理高毒化学品（如苯、DMF、二氯甲烷、汞化合物、氰化物）；2) 处理强渗透性溶剂；3) 混合溶剂体系（不确定性高时选用抗性最好的手套）。层压膜手套通常作为内层，外层戴丁腈手套提供机械保护和抓握力。使用后检查有无破损（针孔测试），可重复使用但需记录使用次数。层压膜手套的缺点是灵活性差、易刺破、成本高。

title: 实验室什么情况下需要戴防割手套？
hazard_types: 割伤;锐器;玻璃碎片
scenario: 防割手套的选择与使用
question: 防割手套（通常为Dyneema或Kevlar材质）用于防止锐器伤害。使用场景：1) 清洗或拆卸玻璃仪器（尤其是磨口粘连时的拆卸）；2) 处理破碎玻璃器皿；3) 使用手术刀片/刀片进行切割操作；4) 安装/更换注射器针头（虽不应回套，但某些必要操作时）。注意：防割手套≠防化手套，不能防化学品渗透。防割手套应在防化手套外层或单独使用（根据是否需要防化）。破损的防割手套应立即更换（防割性能大打折扣）。

title: 激光防护镜应该如何选择？
hazard_types: 激光辐射;眼损伤;可见光/红外/紫外
scenario: 激光防护镜的选择
question: 激光防护镜必须与所用激光器的波长和功率匹配。选择要点：1) 查看激光器的安全标签确认波长（如1064nm Nd:YAG）和等级（Class 3B/4必须佩戴）；2) 防护镜标注光密度（OD值）——OD越高防护能力越强，但透光率越低；3) 不同波长需要不同的防护镜（532nm绿色防护镜对1064nm红外无效！）；4) 飞秒/皮秒超快激光需要特殊宽带防护镜；5) 防护镜镜架上标注适用波长范围，确认涵盖所用激光波长；6) 定期检查镜片有无划痕/褪色/老化。

steps: 确认激光波长和功率→查阅激光器安全标签→选择匹配OD值和波长的防护镜→检查镜片→佩戴→使用后妥善存放

title: 什么情况下需要佩戴面罩？和护目镜有什么区别？
hazard_types: 飞溅;冲击;高温;紫外
scenario: 防护面罩的使用场景
question: 面罩（Face Shield）提供整个面部的防护，但不能替代护目镜！面罩+护目镜组合用于高风险场景：1) 大量强酸/强碱操作（>500mL）；2) 处理自燃或水反应性试剂（如钠、叔丁基锂、LAH）；3) 液氮或干冰/异丙醇浴的操作；4) 高压反应釜开釜操作；5) 打磨/切割操作（需抗冲击面罩）；6) UV消毒灯照射区域清洁（需防紫外面罩）。面罩不能替代护目镜——化学品溅入可能从面罩下方进入眼部，因此面罩下必须佩戴护目镜。

title: 实验室什么时候需要C级化学防护服？正压防护服用在什么场景？
hazard_types: 高毒化学品;感染性气溶胶;缺氧风险
scenario: 正压防护服和C级化学防护服
question: 化学防护服分四级：A级（全封闭气密型，最高防护）> B级（全封闭供气型）> C级（化学防溅服+全面罩空气过滤呼吸器）> D级（普通工作服+基础PPE）。高校实验室最多用到C级。C级适用于：已知化学品浓度不超IDLH值、氧气充足(>19.5%)的环境，如大量化学品泄漏清理、高活性化学品处理。C级需配合全面罩+适当滤毒盒。注意：C级不能用于缺氧环境、未知化学品、或浓度>IDLH的场景。正压防护服（PAPR）用于BSL-3/4生物安全实验室，提供正压空气+全身防护。

title: 操作纳米材料需要什么特殊PPE？
hazard_types: 纳米颗粒;吸入;皮肤渗透;未知毒性
scenario: 纳米材料操作的PPE要求
question: 纳米材料（粒径<100nm）因其极小的尺寸可能通过肺泡进入血液循环或沿嗅觉神经入脑，其毒理学数据通常不完整。操作纳米材料（尤其是干燥粉末）的PPE要求：1) 呼吸防护：N95或P100过滤面罩（纳米颗粒可能穿透普通口罩），在通风柜或粉末称量柜中操作；2) 手部防护：丁腈手套双层，操作后确认无破损；3) 实验服：一次性实验服（纳米颗粒可能附着在纤维间难以洗净）；4) 眼部防护：护目镜（防粉尘）；5) 实验结束后湿式清洁（不可干扫——会使纳米颗粒重新悬浮）。

steps: 在通风柜/粉末称量柜内操作→佩戴N95+呼吸器→双层丁腈手套→一次性实验服→护目镜→实验后湿式清洁台面→正确处理废物

title: 进行动物实验需要哪些PPE？
hazard_types: 动物咬伤;过敏;人畜共患病;麻醉废气
scenario: 动物实验的PPE要求
question: 动物实验PPE根据动物种类和实验类型确定。基本要求：1) 动物设施专用实验服或隔离衣（不可穿出动物房）；2) 手套（咬伤高风险操作——如小鼠灌胃——加戴防咬手套外层）；3) 口罩/呼吸防护：对实验动物过敏者（常见大鼠尿液过敏）需加强呼吸防护；4) 护目镜或面罩；5) 专用鞋或鞋套。特殊场景：使用异氟烷等麻醉气体时——在通风柜或配备废气清除装置的环境中进行；非人灵长类实验——BSL-2+或BSL-3级别PPE。离开动物设施前必须脱除PPE并彻底洗手。

steps: 进入动物设施前换专用隔离衣→戴手套/口罩/护目镜→穿专用鞋→实验操作→脱除PPE→洗手→离开设施
ppe: 隔离衣;手套（防咬外层）;口罩;护目镜;专用鞋/鞋套
forbidden: 禁止将动物设施PPE穿出设施;禁止在动物设施内饮食/吸烟;禁止过敏人员未做额外防护接触过敏原;禁止被咬后不做医疗评估
disposal: 动物尸体/组织冷冻暂存后由专业机构无害化处理;针头/锐器入锐器盒

title: 含氟/氢氟酸的废液怎么处理？
hazard_types: 氟离子;腐蚀性;玻璃腐蚀;毒性
scenario: 含氟废液的安全处置
question: 含氟废液（如含HF、氟化物、含氟有机物的废液）特别危险。处置要求：1) 单独收集——含氟废液可腐蚀玻璃容器，须用PE/PP/PTFE塑料容器；2) 不可与酸性废液混合（HF+强酸释放更多HF气体）；3) 标注「含氟废液」及大致浓度；4) 含氟废液不可用玻璃瓶储存（长期会腐蚀玻璃导致泄漏）；5) HF相关实验中所有接触过HF的溶液（包括清洗液）都视为含氟废液。特别警告：HF中毒有延迟性（小面积接触可能数小时后才出现剧痛），所有含氟操作后洗手并监测皮肤。

steps: 用PE/PP/PTFE容器收集→单独密封保存→标注成分和HF浓度→满容器后交专业HF危废处置单位
ppe: 防酸手套（丁基橡胶或层压膜）;护目镜;面罩;实验服
forbidden: 禁止含氟废液与普通酸碱废液混合;禁止用玻璃容器盛放含氟废液;禁止倒入下水道;禁止敞口存放
disposal: 交有危废处置资质的专业单位（需具备HF处理资质）

title: 含氰化物的废液/废物怎么处理？
hazard_types: 氰化物;剧毒;产生HCN气体
scenario: 含氰化物废液的安全处置
question: 氰化物为剧毒物质，其废弃物处置安全要求极高：1) 含氰化物废液必须单独收集于专用废液桶（标注「含氰-剧毒」）；2) 绝对不可与任何酸性废液混合——氰化物遇酸释放HCN剧毒气体（一个呼吸即可致死）；3) 含氰化物废液桶存放在通风良好处；4) 废液桶保持密封；5) 氧化法预处理（漂白水/次氯酸钠在碱性条件下将CN⁻氧化为无害的氰酸根CNO⁻），但此项操作只能由经过专门培训的人员在通风柜内进行；6) 未经脱毒的含氰废液交专业危废单位处置。

title: 老旧设备中可能含有多氯联苯(PCBs)，应该如何识别和处置？
hazard_types: 多氯联苯;持久性有机污染物;致癌
scenario: 含PCBs废物处置
question: 多氯联苯(PCBs)是持久性有机污染物(POPs)，在老旧设备中可能存在。高PCBs风险设备：旧变压器油（1979年前）、旧电容器、旧荧光灯镇流器、旧显微镜浸油、旧导热油。若发现疑似含PCBs的老旧设备：1) 不要擅自拆卸或排油；2) 联系EHS进行PCBs检测（使用Cl-N-Oil试纸或送样分析）；3) 确认含PCBs后，设备和油均须按PCBs危废特殊规定处置（高温焚烧破坏）；4) PCBs泄漏区域需专业清理（PCBs可渗入混凝土并长期残留）；5) 含PCBs废物的处置需专门资质和转运许可。

steps: 识别疑似含PCBs设备→不擅自拆卸→联系EHS检测→确认后由专业人员处置→设备/油交PCBs专业处置单位

title: 实验室产生的放射性废物应该怎么处理？

scenario: 放射性废物的安全处置
question: 放射性废物处置受严格监管：1) 所有放射性废物（固体/液体/闪烁液/动物尸体）必须按核素种类和活度分类收集——短半衰期（如³²P, t₁/₂=14天）和长半衰期（如¹⁴C, t₁/₂=5730年）分开；2) 短半衰期废物暂存至活度衰变至本底水平后按非放射性废物处理（通常存放10个半衰期后检测）；3) 长半衰期废物交放射性废物处置机构；4) 含混合废物（同时含放射性和化学毒性，如闪烁液——含有机溶剂+放射性核素）需双重分类处置；5) 放射性废物暂存库有严格的辐射安全管理和保安措施。放射性废物管理必须在RSO指导下进行。

title: 实验室危废桶上的标签应该怎么填写？
hazard_types: 危废标识错误;信息缺失;法规不合规
scenario: 危险废物标签的正确填写
question: 危废标签必须完整准确填写，否则属于违规。必须标注的信息：1) 废物名称（不可只写「废液」——应写「含二氯甲烷的卤代有机废液」或更具体）；2) 主要成分及浓度（至少列出主要有害成分）；3) 危险特性（腐蚀性/毒性/易燃性/反应性）；4) 产生日期（开始收集的日期）；5) 产生实验室/房间号；6) 负责人姓名和联系方式；7) 危废类别代码。使用防水标签，用签字笔填写（不可用铅笔或可擦笔）。标签贴于废液桶侧面显眼位置，不可贴在桶底或桶盖上。满桶或过期未清理的及时联系危废转运。

title: 发现无标签的未知化学品应该如何处理？为什么不能随便丢弃？
hazard_types: 未知化学品;意外反应;爆炸;毒气;法律风险
scenario: 无标签/未知化学品的处置流程
question: 未知化学品是所有实验室危废中最危险、最昂贵的一类。为什么不能丢弃：1) 不同化学品混合可能反应（产热/产气/爆炸/释放毒气）；2) 危废处置公司需知道废物成分才能确定处置方法和收费——未知废物需先花数千元做分析鉴定；3) 某些化学品（如含PCBs、二噁英前体）需特殊许可处置。处置流程：1) 仍在原瓶中的未知化学品：查实验室录入记录/采购记录试图追溯；2) 若无法确定：在瓶身标注「未知物-勿动-待鉴定」；3) 不移动不开盖；4) 联系EHS安排专业鉴定和处置；5) 若已泄漏或产生异味：疏散区域，通风，报告应急响应。

title: 生物安全等级BSL-1到BSL-4的区别是什么？实验室如何确定自己的BSL等级？
hazard_types: 生物危害;病原体;感染
scenario: BSL-1到BSL-4的区别
question: 生物安全等级(BSL)按病原体的传染性和致死性分为四级。BSL-1：已知不引起健康成人疾病的微生物（如非致病性大肠杆菌K12株），基础防护（实验服+手套+洗手），开放实验台操作。BSL-2：引起人类疾病但通常可治疗的病原体（如金黄色葡萄球菌、乙肝病毒），需生物安全柜(BSC)操作感染性材料、限制进入、锐器管理、高压灭菌。BSL-3：可通过气溶胶传播的严重/致死性病原体（如结核分枝杆菌、SARS-CoV-2），需负压实验室、BSC或隔离器内操作、呼吸防护、严格控制进入。BSL-4：极高致死率且无疫苗/治疗方法的病原体（如埃博拉病毒），全身正压防护服、完全隔离实验室、多重气锁门、化学淋浴。中国采用与WHO/CDC一致的四级体系。高校教学实验室最多到BSL-2。

steps: 进行风险评估→确定所需BSL等级→配备相应设施和PPE→制定SOP→培训→定期审查生物安全

disposal: 按相应BSL等级要求灭活和处置生物废物

title: 如何确保高压灭菌真的灭了菌？灭菌失败会有什么后果？
category: 高压灭菌生物废物验证
hazard_types: 生物危害;灭菌失效;感染风险
scenario: 高压灭菌效果的验证
question: 高压灭菌（121°C, 15psi, 30分钟）是生物废物灭活最常用方法，但灭菌可能失败。失败原因：1) 包装太紧——蒸汽不能穿透到内部；2) 袋内空气未排出——空气隔热阻碍蒸汽接触；3) 灭菌时间不足——对大量液体或密集固体废物需延长灭菌时间；4) 灭菌锅维护不良——温度计/压力表不准。验证方法：(a) 化学指示带（每袋必贴，灭菌后变色）——基础验证；(b) 生物指示剂（含嗜热脂肪芽孢杆菌Geobacillus stearothermophilus孢子）——每月至少做一次，56°C培养48h后检查有无生长，这是验证灭菌效果的黄金标准；(c) 定期进行灭菌锅性能测试（Bowie-Dick测试等）。灭菌失败的废物必须重新灭菌，不可按已灭活处理。

disposal: 灭活后废物按普通垃圾或非感染性生物废物处置

title: 做细胞培养实验需要遵守哪些生物安全规定？
hazard_types: 细胞培养污染;支原体;病毒;交叉污染
scenario: 细胞培养中的生物安全
question: 细胞培养是生物实验室最常见操作，生物安全要点：1) 所有来源的人和灵长类细胞系按BSL-2处理（可能携带血源性病原体如HIV/HBV）；2) 已知污染或未鉴定的细胞系也按BSL-2；3) 所有细胞培养操作在生物安全柜内进行（保护样品+保护人员）；4) 进入培养室前消毒双手；5) 培养瓶/皿表面用70%乙醇擦拭后方可放入培养箱；6) 废弃培养物（旧培养基、细胞悬液）不可直接倒入下水道（需化学消毒或高压灭菌后处置）；7) 定期检测支原体污染；8) 定期用DNA指纹验证细胞系身份（防交叉污染和误认）。液氮保存的细胞冻存管应使用可耐液氮温度的专用冻存管。

title: 使用含抗生素抗性基因的质粒或微生物时需要注意什么？
category: 微生物耐药性基因操作安全
hazard_types: 抗生素抗性基因;GMO;环境释放;水平基因转移
scenario: 含抗生素抗性基因的微生物实验安全
question: 抗生素抗性基因（ARGs）是生物安全的重要关切：1) 含ARGs的重组微生物（如含氨苄抗性基因的大肠杆菌）属于基因修饰生物(GMO)，需按GMO法规管理；2) 此类微生物不可故意释放到环境中（ARGs可能通过水平基因转移扩散到环境微生物）；3) 所有含ARGs的培养物、废液、污染耗材灭活后（高压灭菌或化学消毒）方可丢弃；4) 在生物安全柜内操作以防止气溶胶扩散；5) 含ARGs菌株的保藏和转移需记录并遵守GMO转移规定；6) 使用环境样本做受体菌时注意——环境菌比实验室菌更容易在环境中存活和扩散ARGs。

title: 被沾有血液或体液的针头刺伤后应该怎么办？
hazard_types: 血源性病原体;HIV;HBV;HCV;针刺伤
scenario: 血液/体液职业暴露后的处理
question: 这是实验室最严重的职业暴露之一。立即处理步骤：1) 挤压伤口使血液流出（促进排出），然后用流动水和肥皂彻底清洗至少5分钟；2) 用碘伏或70%乙醇消毒伤口；3) 不要包扎过紧。立即报告和就医：1) 报告实验室负责人和职业卫生部门；2) 尽快（最好2小时内）到指定医疗机构进行暴露后评估；3) 需要检测患者源（如已知）的HIV/HBV/HCV感染状态；4) 如果源患者HIV阳性或未知，暴露后预防(PEP)应在暴露后1-2小时内开始，最迟不超过72小时，持续服药28天；5) 检测基线HIV/HBV/HCV抗体，并在6周、3个月、6个月复查；6) 暴露后预防服药期间和之后6个月内采取安全措施防止传播。

title: 在放射性同位素实验室工作需要遵守哪些基本规则？

scenario: 放射性同位素实验室的基本安全规则
question: 放射性实验室工作遵循ALARA原则（合理可行尽量低，As Low As Reasonably Achievable）。减少辐射暴露三原则：时间（缩短照射时间）、距离（增大与放射源的距离——辐射强度与距离平方成反比）、屏蔽（使用适当屏蔽材料：β射线用有机玻璃/塑料、γ/X射线用铅/混凝土）。基本规则：1) 进入控制区前佩戴个人剂量计；2) 所有操作在指定辐射区内进行；3) 放射性物质标记清晰（核素+活度+日期）；4) 双手离开放射源后用辐射检测仪检测手套和实验台；5) 食饮化妆品严禁在辐射区内；6) 怀孕或计划怀孕人员需特别评估并调整剂量限值；7) 废弃物严格分类管理。
